title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the Committee's 2020 report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its commitment to addressing key concerns such as transparency, accountability, and safety in AI deployment. It proposes regulatory measures and collaborative efforts with stakeholders to ensure AI technologies align with public interest and ethical guidelines.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the European Union's 2024/1689 regulation on artificial intelligence, outlining new harmonised rules and changes to existing regulations and directives. It serves as the government's overview of how the law will impact AI development, use, and compliance across member states.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual will create clear rules to guide the use of AI tools in the qualifications sector, ensuring that exams remain fair, transparent, and secure. The regulator will work with educational bodies, technology experts and industry partners to develop guidelines, monitor compliance, and keep public confidence in the integrity of qualifications.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected works are used to train and build AI systems, assessing the legal and ethical consequences for creators, rights holders, and AI developers. It provides an impact analysis and recommends strategies to balance innovation with respect for intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” by outlining steps to strengthen regulation and support innovation. It aims to balance safeguarding public interests while maintaining the country’s competitive edge in artificial intelligence.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope, responsibilities, and objectives for a committee that will review how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards. It also provides frequently asked questions to help guide the committee’s discussion and decision‑making process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission discusses how AI should be regulated, focusing on accountability, transparency, and safety measures.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This document examines how artificial intelligence is changing the rules and oversight for medical products, aiming to ensure safety and effectiveness. It outlines how the AI White Paper principles will be applied to create clearer, more consistent guidelines for developers and regulators.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a vision for the organisation to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI-driven defence force among similarly sized entities. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities, fostering responsible use, and strengthening partnerships to maintain a strategic advantage.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport (DfT) will partner with the transport sector to harness AI’s benefits. It also sets out measures to identify and manage the risks that could arise from using AI technologies in transport.
